title: Lucky Thompson gets his notice; his attitude and exile
summary: Lucky showed up with a clarinet and was fired; Cobb says his attitude blocked bookings and drove him to Europe, whereas it is best to be congenial.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: What happened to -- what happened as far as the upbeat on the horn was concerned? What did he do?
Well, he finally got his notice.
And never got the horn?

I had it. So he come in with clarinet. But he goes to show them up. I'm going to sell my horn off, and I'll come with a clarinet until you get my horn from them, but they didn't get it for them. So Hamp said, s-s-s-s-s-- gave -- and they gave him his notice.
Well (inaudible).
No, I just put that (inaudible).
Oh, I'm sorry. No, but why I asked
you about that was, you know, I knew he was like this later, but I didn't know when he --
Was like that then.
Oh, it must have been --
Didn't have but three years of experience on the horn.
That's strange because, you know, in some ways Lucky's very nice.

See, he's one of the guys that I taught that Lady Be Good to, and he'd catch on very fast, got a good, sharp mind, you know. But he had an attitude because I was giving it to him, so I -- you know, I'd been a fixture in the band for a while, so it didn't bother me.
But it -- you know, it seems to me as though Lucky was his own worst enemy really.
That's right.
You know, I know, you know when --
That's why he had to leave and go to Europe.

Yeah, because he -- I mean a lot of the things he said and did were -- were right in a way. We know the business was rotten. We know agents take advantage and everything, but still and all you have to be careful you're not cutting off your nose to spite your face.
And that's what he did. And behind that

he lost his wife. She passed. And he'd begin to say, here, now, he's back in New York, and he's doing fine. I tell you who loved him really, Archie Moore really loved Lucky. He was willing to put some money behind him and everything to make him go.

And he come to see me when I was flat on my back from my final operation, when I was living in Long Island at the time. And he was (inaudible) -- and he's just like Lucky's (inaudible). You know how you can get?
Is that right?
Yeah.
And he put money back of him?
No, he didn't. But he was willing to.
Yeah, I understand.

But by this time Lucky was getting ready to leave out of the country because he had -- you know, you can overtalk yourself and treat people wrong, and no booking office in New York would touch him from his attitude. See, you got to play ball sometime. You got to be a nice guy sometime, especially if your foot ain't in the door. But once you get your foot in the door, you might be able to open it. That's what I'm saying. It's best to be congenial.
They tell me the meek -- from the Bible -- said the meek will inherit the earth. So there ain't no use of being a prima donna right away. Okay.
